QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_2

question.text: Swasth Bharat Trust has asked Mr. Arjun Desai (Cost Accountant, SIA on empanelment waitlist) to comment on the order of elements in its Logic Model. Which of the following represents the CAUSAL IMPLEMENTATION flow — i.e., the order in which value is created on the ground, as conceptually supported by p. 140 of the SIA workbook (resources are deployed first; long-term impact emerges last)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Conceptually supported by p. 140 of the SIA workbook, the CAUSAL implementation flow of a Logic Model runs from Inputs (resources deployed) -> Activities (tasks performed) -> Outputs (deliverables) -> Outcomes (immediate/intermediate changes) -> Impact (long-term consequences). Option D captures this causal chain exactly. The Trap: Option A is the PRESENTATION order in Chapter 4.3 (p. 94), which lists the Logic Model top-down starting from Impact when describing the hierarchy of result statements. That reverse-listed presentation order is what makes A defensible if the stem asks for the chapter's listing order; the audit flagged this as the source of ambiguity. Options B and C scramble the sequence and are not supported under either reading. Note: The original stem said "the correct flow as per the chapter" without specifying causal flow vs the chapter's top-down listing order. Because Chapter 4.3 on p. 94 actually presents the elements in the reverse order (Impact at the top), option A could be defended as the chapter's listing order while option D is the causal flow. The stem has been narrowed to ask for the CAUSAL IMPLEMENTATION flow, making option D uniquely correct, and the explanation no longer mis-references option B as the causal chain.
